anti_overlap: Does not evaluate whether tonal-theme is the right taxonomy axis or whether five is a well-calibrated wing count for literacy cadence — that is fd-taxonomy-legibility-design's remit.

Does not evaluate whether the current Encryptid data type or jawnomicon import pipeline can carry a family/wing field, or whether hatch-mapping and loot-literacy pull toward different taxonomies — that is fd-dataflow-dual-consumer's remit.
Does not review PixiJS rendering, zone-shaping, or persistence mechanics of Beat 1/Beat 2, which are out of scope for the wing-bias composition question.
decision_lens: If the wing-bias / kill-share-heredity / playstyle-axis composition were implemented literally as the brainstorm describes it, would any legal run-signature combination be capable of producing a wing-appropriate hatch with truly zero probability — a hard gate, which the goal explicitly rules out — and is the actual weighting arithmetic specified precisely enough to build, or does 'compose... so hatches stay legible but not deterministic' remain an unspecified aspiration?
focus: How wing bias should compose with the roster kill-share heredity signal and the pace/aggression/thoroughness playstyle axes without hard-gating the 645-creature roster, evaluated against this project's own established ARPG-itemization canon for soft bias versus hard gates.
name: fd-loot-bias-composition
persona: Apply the perspective of an ARPG loot-and-itemization systems designer experienced in soft-bias mechanics that shape drop or match probability without ever fully excluding outcomes — Path of Exile's influence-tagging and league-mechanic weighting, Diablo's affix-weight tables, and this project's own ruled-and-shipped 'no magic-find stat, ever' (delve-formation §11.4) and 'influence rides the mass, never the map' (teardown-arpg-modifiers §12.1) precedents — someone who treats every proposed multi-signal composition as a weighting function that must be specified (what's additive, what's multiplicative, what's a hard filter) rather than accepting a verb like 'biases' or 'composes' left unspecified.
review_areas: Hard-gate risk: does any reading of decision 9's 'wing grammar → creature family pool' (a 'pool' restrict, not a weight) amount to a de facto hard filter — i.e. can the matcher only draw candidates from the rolled wing's family list, making off-wing creatures literally unreachable that run — and if so does that contradict the goal's explicit 'never hard-gate the 645-creature roster' requirement and the project's own no-magic-find precedent (§11.4)?

Composition arithmetic: is there an actual specified function (additive score bonus, multiplicative weight, softmax reweighting, top-K pool restriction with an escape valve) for combining wing bias with kill-share heredity and the pace/aggression/thoroughness playstyle axes, or is 'compose... legible but not deterministic' left as an unimplemented aspiration with no worked numeric example?

Legibility-vs-randomness tension: given the matcher's current top-3 justification mechanism (`getMatchedDimensions`'s per-dimension distance threshold, plus `RunReport.ts`'s roster/kill-share display), would a soft-weighted composition of three signals still produce a top-3 whose 'why it matched' reasoning reads as legible to the player, or does stacking three probabilistic nudges wash out into noise the player can't parse?

Existing precedent fidelity: does the proposed composition mechanism resemble a mechanism this project has already ruled on and shipped for a structurally similar problem (Eidolon influence's pack-density soft-bias, §12.1-§12.2 — 'influence rides the mass, never the map'), or does it invent new machinery where reusing the established shape would be lower-risk and more consistent with shipped canon?

Roster-reachability math: given the straw wings' uneven family-pool sizes (45-63 members per wing by direct count against the real family data) if implemented as weighted pools, does any proposed weighting scheme risk starving whichever signal composes last — i.e. does order-of-operations (wing bias applied before vs. after kill-share/playstyle reweighting) change which creatures remain practically reachable?

Playstyle-axis grounding: do the 'pace/aggression/thoroughness' playstyle axes referenced as an existing hatch signal correspond to anything the delve sim actually tracks per run today, or is the composition question being posed about signals that don't yet exist in `RunReportSource` (which currently exposes only presence-kind/tint/mods/kills, `waveReached`, `runKills`, `elapsedTime`, `echoShards`, `dropsCollected`) — note that 'aggression' does exist in the codebase, but only as a per-creature `Personality` trait inside the habitat sim, not as a run-level playstyle metric.

severity_examples.condition: the wing→family-pool language in decision 9 is carried into implementation as a candidate-set restriction rather than a score-space weight, with no residual/escape-valve pool for off-wing creatures.
severity_examples.scenario: Decision 9 ('wing grammar → creature family pool') is implemented as a hard filter — the matcher only scores candidates drawn from the rolled wing's family list — which silently violates the goal's explicit 'never hard-gate the 645-creature roster' constraint and reproduces exactly the kind of deterministic gate the project's own no-magic-find ruling (§11.4) was written to prevent elsewhere in the loot system.

severity_examples.condition: no worked numeric example or scoring formula appears anywhere in the decisions or open-questions sections for combining the three signal types.
severity_examples.scenario: Open questions 2 and 4 (exactly which run facts map to which matcher axes; how a hatched creature's traits generate its presence spec) remain explicitly unresolved, but decision 9 already asserts wing bias, kill-share heredity, and playstyle axes will 'compose' — no arithmetic is specified anywhere for how three signals combine into one candidate score, so the design cannot be implemented without an unstated judgment call at build time about additive vs. multiplicative weighting, and different implementers would plausibly land on differently deterministic-feeling answers.

severity_examples.condition: the justification UI is scoped to reuse `getMatchedDimensions`'s existing per-dimension distance-threshold logic unmodified once wing/kill-share/playstyle terms are added to the score.
severity_examples.scenario: The pick-of-3 justification screen (decision 9's 'shown at hatch... says why each candidate matched') is scoped against a matcher whose actual scoring is a 28-axis weighted-distance function plus a hash-derived pseudo-random fallback for four dimensions (`hashToFloat` feeding 'Metaphysical Inclination', 'Technology Orientation', 'Curiosity', 'Loyalty') — layering a wing-bias term, a kill-share term, and a playstyle term on top of that without redesigning the explanation string risks a top-3 whose stated 'reasons they matched' reads as three internally-plausible but mutually incoherent justifications rather than one legible story.

success_hints: Distinguishes explicitly between a 'pool restriction' (hard gate) and a 'score weighting' (soft bias) reading of decision 9's language, and states which one the brainstorm's other constraints actually require.

Cites the project's own precedent (§11.4 no-magic-find, §12.1 influence-rides-the-mass) as the bar the composition mechanism should be checked against, rather than a generic ARPG-design abstraction disconnected from this codebase's rulings.
Checks whether 'pace/aggression/thoroughness' playstyle axes have any grounding in what `RunReportSource` or the delve sim currently emits, rather than assuming they are already-available signals.
Proposes (or explicitly asks for) a concrete worked example — an actual formula or decision table — for how the three signals combine, not just a restatement that they should 'compose... legibly.'

Distinguishes whether the composition question is a genuine Beat-1 blocker versus something legitimately answered by the plan-level open questions the brainstorm already lists (#2, #4), without inventing a duplicate open question.
task_context:
Ideate and evaluate alternatives for the Borgesroom wing-set v0 in After Them — the themed wing identity each delve run rolls, which biases the encryptid matcher's family pools and makes run→creature hatching legible ('this run became this creature'). The current straw proposal is five tonal wings mapped to jawnomicon families: Funerary (Death-Criers/Underworld Court/Night-Comers), Tempest (Tempest-Bringers/Rain-Serpents/Rain-Holders/Maelstrom-Makers), Hearth (Hearth-Bound/Kindly Watchers/Blessing-Bearers/First Teachers), Hungers (Lurking Hunters/Hungers That Think/Monstrous Broods/Wings of Ill Omen), Mirrors (Tricksters/Shape-Thieves/Never-Caught). Evaluate and propose better alternatives on four questions: (1) Is wing-as-tonal-theme the right taxonomy axis at all? Consider alternatives: wings by record type (canon §11.6: 'funerary wings lean funerary records' — wings are archive sections of a Borgesian library), by eidogen dimension cluster, by media-feature region (entropy/rhythm/emotionalTone), by enemy ecology, by player-verb affordance. (2) Is five the right count for Beat 1, given each wing must be felt often enough to build literacy? (3) How should wing bias compose with the other hatch signals (roster kill-share heredity, pace/aggression/thoroughness playstyle axes) so hatches stay legible but not deterministic — and never hard-gate the 645-creature roster? (4) The wings will serve TWO consumers — hatch mapping now, loot-farming literacy later (§11.6) — do the two jobs pull toward different taxonomies, and if so which taxonomy serves both? Ground in the actual sources, do not trust summaries: docs/research/2026-08-09-meta-home-loop-teardowns.md, game-design-docs/teardown-arpg-modifiers.md §11-12, game-design-docs/after-them-delve-formation.md (R1-R8), /Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/exports/families/v16/families.json (44 families with member lists), /Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/data/families-prose.yaml (family blurbs), src/sim/habitat/types.ts (MediaFeatures), src/sim/habitat/encryptidMatcher.ts (scoring), src/ui/RunReport.ts (available run facts).

Grounding for this lens: read `game-design-docs/teardown-arpg-modifiers.md` §11.3-11.6 (no-magic-find rule, L4 economy phasing, the §11.6 Borgesroom-literacy passage this whole design descends from) and §12.1-12.3 (Eidolon influence's soft-bias-not-gate mechanism, and its explicit 'the rooms never change, the fauna changes' framing) as the canon bar. Read `src/sim/habitat/encryptidMatcher.ts` in full — it is the actual scoring function question 3 asks you to reason about, and it currently has zero concept of family or wing; any composition proposal has to say where in that file's scoring pipeline the new terms enter. Read `src/ui/RunReport.ts`'s `RunReportSource`/`RunReportData` interfaces for the literal set of run facts available today before asserting a playstyle axis is 'available.'
